summary: Manitoba Historical Society lists the Sasaginnigak fire tower, beside Sasaginnigak Lake in Atikaki Provincial Park, as one of the last standing; no build date found.

visit.trail_note: A lodge on the lake advertises a hike to the fire tower. No source found describes the trail or access rules.

events.note: A 1933 newspaper item, quoted on the Canada's Fire Lookouts site, describes a forestry lookout station at Lake Sasaginnigak. It does not say whether that station was this tower.

evidence.supports: Lookout towers once common in Manitoba; most have been removed
evidence.quote: Fire lookout towers were once commonly used to watch for forest fires in Manitoba but most of them have been removed.

evidence.supports: One of the last towers still standing, beside Sasaginnigak Lake in Atikaki Provincial Park
evidence.quote: One of the last towers to remain standing is found beside Sasaginnigak Lake in Atikaki Provincial Park.

evidence.supports: Photo of the tower dated May 2018
Page revised 28 October 2018, the latest date on the description
1933 item: forestry lookout station at Lake Sasaginnigak; carrier pigeon message of 14 hours of rain to Lac du Bonnet
evidence.quote: The bird, flying from the forestry lookout station at Lake Sasaginnigak to the base station at Lac du Bonnet, bore a message telling of a 14 hours rain.

evidence.supports: Rain had banished the fire menace in the area, per forestry officials
evidence.quote: Heavy rainfall east of Lake Winnipeg during the last few days has banished the menace of forest fires in that area, forestry officials stated today.

evidence.supports: Lodge advertises a hike to the fire tower with views over the lake
evidence.quote: Hiking the trail to the fire tower offers an expansive view of the lake from a great vantage point.
The glad tidings were conveyed Tuesday by a carrier pigeon

sources.title: Sasaginnigak Fire Tower (Sasaginnigak Lake, Atikaki Provincial Park)
sources.publisher: Historic Sites of Manitoba, Manitoba Historical Society

sources.title: Sasaginnigak (quotes a 1933 Winnipeg Free Press item)

notes_for_editor: No build date, builder, height or design found in any source read. The brief's agency (Manitoba Wildfire Service) is not named in any source read, so it is not in facts. Access is undescribed beyond a lodge's marketing line, so no access key was written. The 1933 'lookout station' may or may not be this tower; the story does not link them. The MHS page is the only description of the tower itself and is dated to a 2018 photo. Coordinates in the brief match the MHS page (N51.60048, W95.67231).
